summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to coat tungsten woodpile photonic crystals with iridium to modify their optical properties. The ALD process involves the use of iridium precursor and molecular oxygen as reactants. The coating allows for a shift in the photonic band edge to shorter wavelengths, enabling better control over the optical properties of the structure for high-temperature applications.
evidence: Atomic-layer-deposited iridium is coated onto three-dimensional tungsten woodpile photonic crystals to modify the optical properties of the structure. ... The deposition utilized the reactants tris(2,4-pentanedionato) iridium and molecular oxygen. ... The substrate was held at 250° C.
